plot: Odo and Mothwick follow the true case of the Man in the Iron Mask: a prisoner arrested in July 1669 and named 'Eustache Dauger' is kept masked by the same jailer, Saint-Mars, for 34 years until he dies in the Bastille on 19 November 1703 and is buried as 'Marchioly'; Voltaire and Dumas turn him into the king's iron-masked brother or twin, but the twist is that the jailers' own records describe a black velvet mask and call him only a valet, who had once served the fallen minister Fouquet.

script.title: Who Was Behind the Iron Mask?

beats.say: 1703, Paris. A prisoner died in the Bastille. Nobody knew his face.
Nobody? Not even his guards? Mothwick, somebody must have known.
For thirty-four years, a mask hid his face from the world.
This one is true, Odo. The jailers' letters still exist.
July 1669. A man was arrested near Calais, on the king's orders.
The minister's letter gave his name as Eustache Dauger.
So they knew his name! Then the mystery is solved.
A name, Odo. Not who he was, or what he knew.
I am Saint-Mars, his jailer. Only I may speak with him.
The orders were strict. He could speak only of his daily needs.
If he said anything else, he was to be killed.
Killed for talking? What could a prisoner know?
At Pignerol, in the Alps, he was made a servant.
He waited on another prisoner there, a fallen minister, Nicolas Fouquet.
Remember that, Odo. A servant, in a room full of secrets.
Saint-Mars moved from prison to prison. The prisoner always went with him.
A prisoner who follows his jailer? Like a shadow.
Pignerol. Then Exilles. Then an island off the coast near Cannes.
Always the same jailer? For almost thirty years?
September 1698. Saint-Mars became governor of the Bastille, in Paris.
An officer, Etienne du Junca, kept a register as they arrived.
An old prisoner, always masked, whose name is not spoken.
Remember one small word in that register. Velvet.
Velvet? Why would one word matter, Mothwick?
On the nineteenth of November, 1703, he felt unwell after mass.
He died that same evening, without any serious illness.
Next day he was buried under a false name: Marchioly.
Even his grave, Odo, got a name that was not his.
Subscribe for a new true story every day. Now the strangest part.
In 1717, a young writer called Voltaire was locked in the Bastille.
A masked prisoner, for a lifetime? I must know who he was.
Later Voltaire wrote that the mask was iron, and the man royal.
An iron mask for thirty-four years? That's horrible!
Voltaire guessed he was the king's secret elder brother.
The king's own brother, locked away in iron?
In 1850, Alexandre Dumas made him the king's identical twin.
Its last part became famous as The Man in the Iron Mask.
A secret twin! That's why they hid his face!
Think, Odo. Remember the word in the register.
Velvet. Du Junca wrote velvet. Not iron.
Yes. His death entry speaks of a mask of black velvet.
The iron came from a legend. The twin came from a novel.
And the minister's letter called Dauger only a valet. A servant.
A servant? Then why hide a servant for thirty-four years?
The servant of Fouquet, Odo. He may have heard too much.
Many historians think so. Nobody has ever proven it.
Only his jailer knew for sure. And Saint-Mars never told.
The man in the iron mask wore velvet, and kept his secret.
If this one got you, the Strasbourg dancing plague story is next.
Have you heard a story like this one? Tell me in the comments.

long.title: 1703: Who Was Behind the Iron Mask? | True Story Animated
long.description:
Previous true story: https://youtu.be/gNRPXe-J4dU
Have you heard a story like this one? Tell me in the comments.

"He wore that mask for thirty-four years, and kept his secret." — Odo

A true story from the Bastille, Paris: on 19 November 1703 a prisoner died who had been kept masked since 1669, always guarded by the same jailer, Saint-Mars, and was buried under a false name, 'Marchioly'. Voltaire said the mask was iron and the man royal; Alexandre Dumas made him the king's twin. But the prison's own register speaks of a mask of black velvet, and the minister's letter calls him only a valet.
